sources.title: Register with the authorities: degree students | Instructions | Studies Service | University of Helsinki
highlights:
When your studies in Finland last over a year, you should register with a municipality of residence (domicile) at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV).

- Acquiring a permanent address and place of domicile entitles you to enjoy municipal benefits, including a student discount with HSL (public transport) and the right to use municipal health care (if your studies last at least two years).
- By registering in the Finnish Population System you will also receive a personal identity code, assuming you haven’t been assigned it by Migri.
- The personal identity code is compulsory to have in case your stay lasts at least three months (obliged by the University of Helsinki) and it is needed for various services in Finland, eg. opening a bank account.
- Please see here below citizenship specific guidelines.

To register at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency you need to first apply for registration online. When you visit DVV you must have with you:

- your valid passport or EU citizen’s official identity card with a photograph
- your residence permit card or some other proof that you have entered Finland legally
- certificate of student status (can be obtained from your Sisu profile)

Visit the Digital and Population Data Services Agency's website for more information and to book an appointment. We recommend that you book an appointment already before hand from abroad.

Please note that DVV and Migri (the Finnish Immigration Service) will be present at the Check-In Event and you should register with them there, unless you arrive well before or after the Check-In Event.

Once you have received your Finnish personal identity code ("Henkilötunnus" in Finnish) please remember to update it in the student register. You can do it by sending your code from your helsinki.fi email address to international-studentinfo@helsinki.fi.s (the .s is for secure mail).

...

1. Citizens of EU/EEA countries do not need a residence permit or visa, but you need to first apply for EU registration at the Finnish Immigration Service Migri and then register with a municipality of residence (domicile) at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV). When you apply for your EU registration at Migri, please apply also for a personal identity code at the same time. 

- After you have submitted your form for your EU right of residence, visit Migri to identify yourself. You can either do this at the Check-In Event during Orientation Week or if you arrive earlier in August, book an appointment to Migri before hand.

sources.title: For new degree students | Instructions | Studies Service | University of Helsinki
highlights:
### Register with the authorities: degree students 

 After arriving in Finland you will have to register with a few relevant authorities within a certain period of time. Please book your appointment(s) well in advance of your arrival in Finland.

sources.title: International degree student's journey | Instructions | Studies Service | University of Helsinki
highlights:
You will receive your admission result and the decision on the scholarships granted by the University of Helsinki by email. If you have been accepted, the email you receive from us is an official acceptance letter and is suitable for dealing with various authorities such as immigration etc. This same email will also contain instructions for the next steps for confirming your study place and registering your attendance. Make sure you read our newsletters for incoming international students and attend webinars for accepted students to get to know UH better!

...

#### Registering 

Once you have received a study offer, remember to accept your study place and register as attending for the upcoming academic year. When you register as attending, you will become a member of the Student Union HYY by paying their membership fee. If you are liable to pay for tuition, the University will register you as attending once we have received your tuition fee payment, which contains the HYY membership fee. If you are conditionally accepted, you are first required to fulfill the condition by the deadline. In some cases, you may also register as non-attending or apply to defer the beginning of your studies.

- Guide for accepted students, bachelor’s students
- Guide for accepted students, master’s students

Once you are registered as attending, you can activate your IT user account and start using your University of Helsinki email! If needed, you can then download your certificate of student status in Sisu. You will find instructions for all of this in the Instructions for students, which is the go-to place for any possible information students might be looking for.

...

Kick-start your preparation reading our newsletters for new international degree students. We invite you to commence administrative processes such as applying for a residence permit and getting health insurance as early as possible for a timely arrival. 

You will also receive links to a digital skills course and a pre-arrival course—both of which will help you understand the UH environment better.

...

#### Arriving 

As your journey to the University of Helsinki approaches, we look forward to e-meeting you at the pre-arrival webinar organised for incoming international degree students and invite you to keep yourself updated on the latest student information from the Studies Service (studies.helsinki.fi). If you haven’t done so already, now is the moment to activate your Frank student card and to actively start using your helsinki.fi email account. Please remember that the International Student Advice is here to help you settle in and answer your questions on matters such as registering with the Finnish authorities, opening a bank account, getting student-priced transport tickets, and other topics related to living and studying in Finland.

sources.title: Fresher's Handbook - Top Things to Know for First-Year Students
highlights:
After arriving in Finland, you must register your address at the DVV. You can do it by booking an appointment yourself OR by attending the Check-In Event during the orientation week. It is easier and faster to use the services available at the Check-In Event - you’ll need to have some paperwork ready, but attending this event will significantly speed up the processes. The Check-In Event will be held at the Language Center (Fabianinkatu 26) on 28 & 29 August. Each group will have a specific time during these two days: your tutors will inform you of your group time. For this event, please have these documents ready with you:

● Passport or EU Citizen’s ID card 
● Residence permit (for non-EU/EEA students) or EU Citizen’s registration document (if you have one) 
● Your full address, including the apartment/room number 
● Certificate of student status (go to ‘My Profile’ in your Sisu. In the ‘Study rights’ tab, click ‘Form a certificate of student status’) Depending on your home country, the administration process might be slightly different. If you are: 
● a citizen of Nordic countries, complete the electronic form found in this page (under “I am a citizen of a Nordic country or an EU member state”). This form should be filled before the Check-In Event. 
● a citizen of non-EU/EEA countries, complete the electronic form found in this page (under “I am a citizen of some other country”). This form should be filled before the Check-In Event. Even if you already have your personal identity code in your residence 3 

permit, you should still register to the DVV after your arrival in Finland.

● a citizen of EU/EEA countries, you do not need a residence permit or visa to come to Finland. You must however register their EU-right of residence at the Finnish Immigration Office within their first three months and get a permanent address at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV, used to be called maistraatti). 

Fill in the Online form + make an appointment already now (Migri has very long queues) and visit your chosen immigration service point. If you cannot find an available appointment, look on Thursdays for cancellation spots. The EU registration costs 54€. Register then your permanent address at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency by email. A permanent address is needed in order to receive a degree student's discount for the travel card (HSL), as well as opening a bank account. The permanent address cannot be registered before the student has done the EU registration.

Due to Migri's long queues, which hinder the whole registration process, it’s important to first visit DVV at the Check-In Event or in their office to get a temporary address, which at least gives the student the right to get a local's travel card prices.

Important: Up to seven weeks after registering, you will receive your personal identity code via email and/or post. Next, you should inform the International Student Services by sending the last four digits of your personal identity code to international-studentinfo@helsinki.fi.s (s. is for secure mail) from your university email. You should not send your full name and identity code by normal email. You cannot access some services before completing this last step, such as logging in to your student health service account.
